trial_court: Court of Additional District Judge, Muktsar
case_name: Sukhdev Singh vs Chhinder Pal Kaur
facts_of_case: Petitioner's wife filed a petition under Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act alleging that their marriage was null. The court allowed the petition and declared the marriage null. Later, the wife filed another petition under Section 25 of the Hindu Marriage Act claiming maintenance pendente lite. This application was contested by the husband.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage in contravention of Section 5(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act is null and void.
legal_principles.held: Clause (i) of Section 5 lays down, for lawful marriage, the necessary condition that neither party should have a spouse living at the time of the marriage. A marriage in contravention of this condition, therefore, is null and void.
cited_cases: AIR 1988 S.C, 644, Smt. Yamunabai Anantrao Adhav v. Anant Rao Shivram Adhav and another

legal_principles.principle: A void marriage cannot be treated as valid by reference to earlier Hindu Law or custom.
legal_principles.held: The plea that the marriage should not be treated as void because such a marriage was earlier recognised in law and custom cannot be accepted. By reasons of the overriding effect of the Act as mentioned in Section 4, no aid can be taken of the earlier Hindu Law or any custom, or usage as apart of that Law inconsistent with any provision of the Act.
cited_cases: AIR 1988 S.C, 644, Smt. Yamunabai Anantrao Adhav v. Anant Rao Shivram Adhav and another

outcome.final_order: The trial court's order allowing the wife's application for litigation expenses and maintenance pendente lite was upheld.

use_for_drafting: representing clients in nullity of marriage cases
